**📐 Maintainability & Code Quality** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Add the file path to I/O and parse diagnostics.**

`read_source_bytes(source)?`, `std::fs::read(reference)?` and `parse_dataset(...)?` turn an error into a `Diag` without a path. The diagnostic then does not tell the user which of the two input files failed. The existing `lift-r`/`lift-onnx`/`lift-proof` path adds a `Location` and a `gmeow math <leaf>` context frame. Add the same location and context frame to each read and parse call in `Project` and `Lift`.

<details>
<summary>Sketch</summary>

```rust
let at = |path: &Path| move |diag: gmeow_errors::Diag| {
    diag.with_location(gmeow_errors::Location {
        path: Some(path.display().to_string()),
        ..gmeow_errors::Location::default()
    })
    .with_context("gmeow math project")
};
let bytes = read_source_bytes(source).map_err(gmeow_errors::Diag::from).map_err(at(source))?;
```
</details>

**Use the canonical integer to reject a zero matrix denominator.**

`expression::integer_literal` trims XSD whitespace (`' '`, `'\t'`, `'\r'`, `'\n'`) before it parses the literal. The zero check on Line 550 to Line 555 does not trim whitespace. It only strips `+`/`-` and then requires every byte to be `'0'`. A denominator lexical form such as `" 0"` or `"0\n"` passes `integer_literal`. That same value fails the all-zero test. The Data Cube codec then emits an observation with a zero denominator. `expression::number` (Line 224 to Line 228) and `inbound::rational` already compare `canonical_integer(...) == "0"`. Apply the same check here so all three paths agree.

**Do not let a SKOS alignment alone make an external IRI canonical.**

`resolve_symbol` can return the OpenMath IRI unchanged when that IRI is the subject of an `skos:exactMatch` or `skos:closeMatch` row. The callers then emit it as `math:operator` or `math:hasMathematicalSymbol`, without checking the unique native alignment. `Source::extend` preserves input subject direction and performs no symmetric closure.

Remove the SKOS checks from the native branch. Include both `skos:exactMatch` and `skos:closeMatch` in the unique-alignment branch so existing native-subject `closeMatch` mappings remain usable.

**Narrow the `stage-mappings` edge to `graph/alignments`.**

The stage reads only `GRAPH_ALIGNMENTS` from the `stage-mappings` product. The edge is not narrowed, so the persistent cache key covers the whole mappings product. Any edit that changes SSSOM, EDOAL, the lang corpora or the ledger re-runs the ten producers and the seven fixture parity checks. Add a `dataflow_entities` entry, as `st_goal_directed` does. Add the matching `gmeow:BuildDataFlow` edge in `slices/core/pipeline/module.ttl`.

```rust
fn st_math_producers(id: &str, impl_key: &str, consumes: &[&str]) -> StageSpec {
    let mut s = st(id, impl_key, consumes);
    s.dataflow_entities = vec![(
        "stage-mappings".to_string(),
        vec![crate::stages::carrier::GRAPH_ALIGNMENTS.to_string()],
    )];
    s
}
```

**Add a positive check so the lint regression cannot pass vacuously.**

The test only asserts that some errors are absent. Each of the six checks iterates `ds_subjects_of_type(ds, &math_iri("ProjectionRecord"))`. If the lint does not find the generated record under that type IRI, every check skips it and the test still passes. That would happen if the namespace or the record typing drifts between `gmeow_math` and `gmeow_validate`. The hard-coded `math:` prefix at Line 2398 makes this drift more likely. Before running the lint, assert that `combined` contains the `emission.record` subject typed with the IRI that the lint uses.

+        "generated ledger must carry a lint-visible math:ProjectionRecord: {}",
+        emission.ledger
